examples.notes: Two electrically independent three-pass TiN heaters share a larger silicon thermal layer. A and B are biased at 0.4 V and 0.25 V; prescribed loads add 0.5 mW and 0.15 mW respectively. Electrical mode computes each powered net; reported resistance uses A only. Thermal-only mode uses prescribed loads without Joule heating, whereas electrothermal mode adds both Joule loads. Sweep load_a with B held fixed and inspect the rise of B temperature to observe thermal crosstalk. Effective 2e-6 m²K/W interfaces represent omitted isolation stacks; the 5e4 W/m²K backside sink and representative film properties need calibration. Synthetic steady-state 2.5D example.

examples.name: E16_full_gate_hemt_array

catalog.name: E16_full_gate_hemt_array
catalog.title: Full-width gated HEMT array
catalog.learning_goal: Contrast E7's edge bypass with gate control that spans every channel in a four-channel array.
catalog.physical_scope: Resistive 2DEG approximation with finite contacts; no velocity saturation, gate leakage, trapping, or electrostatic field-plate model.

examples.bias_summary: source 0 V (ground); drain 0.1 V (voltage); gate_control 0 V (gate); prescribed heat: channel_load 0.0002 W
examples.notes: Four separated parallel GaN 2DEG stripes join shared source/drain metal buses through finite 1e-10 Ωm² contacts, with 0.1 V drain bias. One gate bar spans each complete channel width, so every source-to-drain channel path crosses a controlled region; there is no ungated edge bypass. The gold gate is electrically insulated and modeled as a thermal-only layer; its voltage enters the local analytical charge-control model through gate_control. No gate leakage, capacitance, electrostatic field solution, velocity saturation or calibrated transistor prediction is provided. A 1e-7 S sheet-conductance floor limits deep-off current and maintains numerical conditioning; the off-state current is not a leakage prediction. A 0.2 mW prescribed channel load supports thermal-only operation and adds to Joule heating in coupled mode. Effective thermal interfaces represent omitted buffer/dielectric paths.

examples.name: E17_pulsed_thermal

catalog.name: E17_pulsed_thermal
catalog.title: Pulsed heating and cooling
catalog.learning_goal: Compare pulse heating and cooling with the uniform lumped thermal RC limit, then refine the time step.
catalog.physical_scope: Prescribed heat drives uniform copper thermal storage; electrical Joule heating is excluded. Pulse width means high plateau.

examples.bias_summary: source 0 V (ground); drain 0 V (voltage); prescribed heat: heater 1e+06 W/m²
examples.waveform_summary: `heat_sources.heater.value`: 0 → 1e+06, delay 0.0001 s, rise 0 s, plateau 0.0002 s, fall 0 s, period 0.0007 s (target SI units).
examples.notes: Uniform prescribed heat pulses in a 100 × 100 × 10 µm copper plate, with h=1e5 W/(m² K). Thermal-only operation excludes Joule heating. The spatially uniform limit has tau=rho*cp*t/h and high-level steady rise=10 K, so the transient can be checked against a lumped RC. Pulse width is the 200 µs plateau, period 700 µs, and delay 100 µs. Reduce dt to check time accuracy.

diagnostics.message: Transient heat flow uses backward Euler and quasi-static electrical states; electrical capacitance, inductance and wave propagation are not modeled.

examples.waveform_summary: `terminals.drain.value`: 0 → 0.25, delay 2.5e-05 s, rise 1e-05 s, plateau 6e-05 s, fall 1e-05 s, period 0.0002 s (target SI units).
